result.summary: Replaces usages of `time.time()` with `time.monotonic()` for interval and timeout calculations across the functional test framework and test runner. This ensures duration measurements are unaffected by system wall-clock adjustments or mocked system time.
result.problem: Functional test timeouts and runtime tracking that rely on wall-clock time (`time.time()`) can experience flakiness or miscalculations whenever the system clock jumps or when tests are executed under time-manipulating tools like `faketime`.
evidence: PR description demonstrates reproducible test failures under faketime: `faketime --exclude-monotonic -f "+0 x0.5" build/test/functional/feature_torcontrol.py` and `faketime --exclude-monotonic -f "+0 x0.1" build/test/functional/interface_http.py`.
PR description references merged PR #36529 as addressing the same class of clock jump flakiness bug.
result.changed_since_previous: None; now evaluated against full patch details.
result.card: Replaces time.time() with time.monotonic() when measuring durations in the functional test framework and test runner. Wall-clock time can jump or skew during test runs or under time-manipulation environments, leading to flaky test failures or inaccurate timeouts. The author demonstrates reproducible test failures under faketime on feature_torcontrol.py and interface_http.py that this change resolves.

risk.why: Mistakes only impact test runner and framework timeout calculations, potentially causing spurious test failures.
